grounding.gloss: condition: a mode of being or form of existence of a person or thing

provenance.evidence: 14288 ongoing-state sentences in v1's count; the residual after the specific types below is what this now covers

item.sense: a general condition the subject is in, not covered by a more specific state type

grounding.gloss: a profession, may involve prolonged training

provenance.evidence: 4357 'i am a <role>', 1830 work-status, 354 student-status and 59 retired sentences: the largest single family of persona content
quit.01 is 'leave your job' and retire.01 'stop working', so employment has its own lifecycle distinct from a generic state change

item.sense: the subject holds, seeks or has left a working or studying position

constraints.expression: this state ends by fulfilment or by l1:event.commitment_withdrawn, and not by the passage of time alone

grounding.gloss: describes a reservation for travel, dining or an event

provenance.evidence: retail order status pending/processed/delivered: the pending case is a state between the commitment and its fulfilment
SYSTEM NOTIFY_SUCCESS 16868 marks the transition out of this state

item.sense: an arrangement is committed to and has not yet been carried out

provenance.evidence: 5307 persona sentences state a possession
own.01 and belong.01 are inverse framings of one owner/possession state

item.sense: the subject has something at their disposal, whether owned or merely held

grounding.gloss: to live for an extended period
entities that have a somewhat fixed, physical extension

provenance.evidence: 1640 residence sentences, of which 59 give a duration ('i have lived there since i was 5')
reside.01's ARG1 is tagged LOC, so the place is a required position rather than an optional detail

item.sense: where the subject lives, as a standing fact with a place the memory can be asked for

grounding.gloss: to make dependent on a condition
a description of an action that is supported

provenance.evidence: condition.01 ARG1 'entity made dependent' is the thing left in this state once the conditioning act is over
472 availability-conditioned requests and 14 'as long as' constraints describe a commitment awaiting a fact the speaker does not yet have

item.sense: a commitment that will take effect only if its trigger condition is met

grounding.gloss: have affection towards, be fond of, enjoy

provenance.evidence: 9517 like/enjoy sentences, the largest affect band and the default reading when no intensifier is present

item.sense: held as a genuine preference without being emphasised

constraints.expression: at most one paramount value may be current per holder and attribute; a second one supersedes the first rather than joining it

grounding.gloss: preference, penchant, predilection, taste: a strong liking

provenance.evidence: 2963 'my favourite/favorite' sentences, a superlative frame distinct from the 4102 love sentences because it excludes ties

item.sense: the single most strongly held option of its kind, admitting no equal

grounding.gloss: intensity, intensiveness: high level or degree

provenance.evidence: 4102 love/adore and 269 hate/can't-stand sentences, plus 104 with an intensifier on a weaker verb ('i really like football')
love.01 and adore.01 are separate rolesets from like.01, so the intensity difference is lexicalized rather than adverbial

item.sense: held strongly enough that the holder volunteers it without prompting

grounding.gloss: tolerate, put up with, the act of tolerating

provenance.evidence: tolerate.01 'put up with' and mind.01 'be bothered by' are distinct rolesets from like.01, so acceptance is a separate attitude rather than weak liking

the weakest band in the corpus: 6 sentences match 'i don't mind' / 'it's ok'. The rank exists because SGD attests it far better -- 14 'as long as' and 472 'if available' utterances are acceptance rather than preference -- but the persona evidence alone would not have carried it
14 utterances state tolerance directly ('any kind of movie is fine, just as long as it's fun')

item.sense: accepted without being preferred, so it may be chosen but will not be sought

provenance.evidence: USER NEGATE_INTENT 5425 abandons rather than revises
56 'i quit / stopped / gave up' sentences
abandon.01 'leave behind' and quit.01 'leave your job' both mark giving up rather than finishing, which achieve.01 covers

item.sense: an intention the subject has given up rather than completed

grounding.gloss: to make dependent on a condition

provenance.evidence: 472 availability-conditioned requests, 88 if/then frames, 14 'as long as'/'only if', 43 'in case'
21 sentence-initial conditionals and 38 'when X i want Y' triggers
condition.01 ARG2 GOL 'dependent on' is the trigger this task waits on

item.sense: an intention the subject will act on only if a stated condition turns out to hold

constraints.expression: an L1 task is what one turn makes explicit; anything requiring evidence from a second turn is an O_L2 abstraction and not this item

grounding.gloss: the act of planning the execution of an event/task to a future date

provenance.evidence: 775 'i want to', 86 'i plan/hope to', 275 'i will / going to' sentences
intend.01 'intend, plan, on purpose' with ARG1 'intent, thing planned'

item.sense: something the subject has said they intend to do, not yet done

constraints.expression: this item ends when the missing value is supplied, so it is not a preference and must not survive its own satisfaction

provenance.evidence: every transactional intent declares required_slots that must be filled before it can be executed
require.01 'need, obligation' ARG1 'thing required' plus need.01

item.sense: something that must be done or supplied before an arrangement can proceed

provenance.evidence: 775 'i want to', 275 'i will/am going to', 94 'someday/one day/in the future'

item.sense: the content is expected or intended to hold later than the assertion

provenance.evidence: 1640 residence and 1830 work-status sentences are stated in present tense as things that are the case now

item.sense: the content holds at the moment of assertion

provenance.evidence: 72 'i moved', 81 'i graduated', 46 'i met': completed events dominate persona narration

item.sense: the content held at a time earlier than the assertion

provenance.evidence: 295 explicit-frequency sentences describe recurrence rather than one occasion

item.sense: the content holds repeatedly rather than once

provenance.evidence: check_in_date/check_out_date and available_start_time/available_end_time are boundary pairs describing one interval
62 'since <point>' sentences state an interval by its start alone

item.sense: the content holds across an interval rather than at a point

provenance.evidence: 4357 'I am a <role>' sentences state a standing fact with no time reference at all

item.sense: the assertion fixes no time and none may be inferred
